source.text: Τότε ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἀνήχθη εἰς τὴν ἔρημον ὑπὸ τοῦ πνεύματος, πειρασθῆναι ὑπὸ τοῦ διαβόλου.

records.literal_gloss: Then the Jesus was led up into the wilderness by the Spirit to be tempted by the devil.

en.L: Then Jesus was led up into the wilderness by the Spirit to be tempted by the devil.
en.B: Then the Spirit led Jesus up into the wilderness, where the devil would tempt {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: Then the Spirit led Jesus into the desert so that the devil could try to make {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} do wrong.

es.L: Entonces Jesús fue conducido arriba, al desierto, por el Espíritu, para ser tentado por el diablo.
es.B: Entonces el Espíritu condujo a Jesús al desierto, donde el diablo {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} iba a tentar.
es.R: Después el Espíritu llevó a Jesús al desierto, para que el diablo tratara de hacer que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} hiciera algo malo.

fr.L: Alors Jésus fut emmené dans le désert par l’Esprit, pour être tenté par le diable.
fr.B: Alors l’Esprit conduisit Jésus au désert, où le diable allait {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} tenter.
fr.R: Ensuite, l’Esprit a conduit Jésus dans le désert. Là, le diable allait essayer de {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} pousser à faire le mal.

sw.L: Kisha Yesu aliongozwa juu hadi nyikani na Roho, ili ajaribiwe na Ibilisi.
sw.B: Kisha Roho alimwongoza Yesu hadi nyikani, ambako Ibilisi angemjaribu.
sw.R: Kisha Roho alimpeleka Yesu jangwani, ili Ibilisi ajaribu kumshawishi atende mabaya.

ko.L: 그때 예수께서 마귀에게 시험을 받으시려고 성령께 이끌려 광야로 올라가셨다.
ko.B: 그때 성령께서 예수를 광야로 이끌고 올라가셨다. 거기서 마귀가 예수를 시험하려는 것이었다.
ko.R: 그 뒤에 성령께서 예수를 빈 들로 데리고 가셨다. 그곳에서 마귀가 예수를 꾀어 죄를 짓게 하려고 했다.

vi.L: Bấy giờ Đức Giê-xu được Thánh Linh dẫn lên đồng hoang để chịu ma quỷ cám dỗ.
vi.B: Bấy giờ Thánh Linh dẫn Đức Giê-xu lên đồng hoang để ma quỷ cám dỗ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Sau đó, Thánh Linh dẫn Đức Giê-xu vào sa mạc để ma quỷ tìm cách khiến {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} làm điều sai.

pt.L: Então Jesus foi conduzido ao deserto pelo Espírito, para ser tentado pelo diabo.
pt.B: Então o Espírito levou Jesus ao deserto, onde o diabo {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} tentaria.
pt.R: Então o Espírito levou Jesus para o deserto, para que o diabo tentasse levá-{{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} a fazer o que é errado.

decisions.choice: tempted: put to the test, here by one who wants him to fail
alternatives: tested, as God tests to prove faithfulness
decisions.reason: The verb covers both testing and tempting. God tested Israel in the wilderness (Deuteronomy 8:2); here the devil tries to lead God's Son away from obedience. The Spirit leads him there, so the trial is within God's purpose.

decisions.choice: the wilderness: where Israel was tested for forty years
decisions.reason: Jesus answers each temptation from Deuteronomy 6-8, where Moses recalls Israel's testing in the wilderness. Where Israel failed, God's Son stays faithful.

decisions.choice: the devil: the slanderer, the enemy of God, also called Satan
alternatives: an evil force with no person behind it
decisions.reason: The Greek word means slanderer or accuser. Matthew also calls him "the tempter" (4:3) and Jesus calls him "Satan" (4:10).

decisions.choice: try to make him do wrong
decisions.reason: Readable says what tempting is.

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B) and the passé composé (R); historic presents kept as presents at Literal ("emmène", "montre", "laisse")
decisions.reason: As in Matthew 1-3 and the other Gospels: the passé simple is the normal tense of written narrative; Readable uses the passé composé, as French is spoken. Speech keeps its own tenses at every level. This holds for the whole chapter.

decisions.choice: le désert at every level; le diable; tenter (L, B), pousser à faire le mal (R) (for the whole book)
decisions.reason: As in Mark and Luke 4: French "le désert" means empty wild land, not only sand, so it serves both the English "wilderness" and Readable's "desert" and keeps the echo of Israel's years there (m2). Readable says what tempting is, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "ma quỷ" for the devil; "cám dỗ" (L, B), "tìm cách khiến Ngài làm điều sai" (R) for tempt
decisions.reason: "Ma quỷ" is the style guide's word for the devil; "cám dỗ" is the usual word for enticing to sin, which is the sense the meaning decision gives here. Readable unfolds it as in Mark 1:13.

decisions.choice: "마귀" for the devil; "시험하다" (L, B), "꾀어 죄를 짓게 하다" (R)
decisions.reason: "마귀" is the word of the Korean John (8:44). "시험" covers both testing and tempting, as the Greek does (meaning decision); Readable says what the tempter wants, as the Korean Mark 1:13 does.

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun spans in Korean, through Matthew 4
decisions.reason: Korean has no capital letters; respect for Jesus is carried by "께서", "그분" and -시- at every level (docs/korean-style.md section 7).

source.text: καὶ νηστεύσας ἡμέρας τεσσεράκοντα καὶ νύκτας τεσσεράκοντα ὕστερον ἐπείνασεν.

records.literal_gloss: And having fasted days forty and nights forty, afterward he was hungry.

en.L: And having fasted forty days and forty nights, afterward {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was hungry.
en.B: He fasted forty days and forty nights, and at the end of it {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was famished.
en.R: He went without food for forty days and forty nights. After that, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was very hungry.

es.L: Y habiendo ayunado cuarenta días y cuarenta noches, después tuvo hambre.
es.B: Ayunó durante cuarenta días y cuarenta noches, y al cabo de ese tiempo tuvo muchísima hambre.
es.R: Estuvo cuarenta días y cuarenta noches sin comer. Después de eso tenía mucha hambre.

fr.L: Et ayant jeûné quarante jours et quarante nuits, ensuite {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} eut faim.
fr.B: Il jeûna quarante jours et quarante nuits, après quoi {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} fut tenaillé par la faim.
fr.R: Il est resté sans manger pendant quarante jours et quarante nuits. Après cela, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait très faim.

sw.L: Na akiisha kufunga siku arobaini na usiku arobaini, baadaye aliona njaa.
sw.B: Alifunga kwa siku arobaini na usiku arobaini, na mwishowe alikuwa na njaa kali.
sw.R: Kwa siku arobaini na usiku arobaini hakula chochote. Baada ya hapo alikuwa na njaa sana.

ko.L: 그리고 사십 일 낮과 사십 일 밤을 금식하신 뒤에, 마침내 배가 고프셨다.
ko.B: 예수께서 사십 일 동안 밤낮으로 금식하셨다. 그러고 나니 몹시 배가 고프셨다.
ko.R: 예수께서는 사십 일 동안 밤낮으로 아무것도 잡수시지 않았다. 그 뒤에 몹시 배가 고프셨다.

vi.L: Và sau khi kiêng ăn bốn mươi ngày và bốn mươi đêm, về sau {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đói.
vi.B: Ngài kiêng ăn suốt bốn mươi ngày bốn mươi đêm, và sau đó {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đói lả.
vi.R: Ngài nhịn ăn trong bốn mươi ngày và bốn mươi đêm. Sau đó, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} rất đói.

pt.L: E, tendo jejuado quarenta dias e quarenta noites, depois teve fome.
pt.B: Ele jejuou quarenta dias e quarenta noites e, no fim, estava faminto.
pt.R: Ele ficou sem comer durante quarenta dias e quarenta noites. Depois disso, estava com muita fome.

decisions.choice: forty days and forty nights: as Moses on the mountain
alternatives: a round number with no echo
decisions.reason: Moses fasted forty days and forty nights before receiving the law (Exodus 34:28; Deuteronomy 9:9), and Elijah traveled forty days and nights to Horeb (1 Kings 19:8). The forty also recalls Israel's forty years in the wilderness.

decisions.choice: afterward he was hungry: weakness that the tempter uses
decisions.reason: The plain words set up the first temptation, which is about bread.

decisions.choice: went without food
decisions.reason: Readable says what fasting is.

decisions.choice: "kiêng ăn" (L, B); "nhịn ăn" (R) for fasting
decisions.reason: "Kiêng ăn" is going without food for a religious purpose; "ăn chay" now means eating no meat, and "tuyệt thực" suggests a hunger strike. Readable uses the everyday "nhịn ăn".

source.text: καὶ προσελθὼν ὁ πειράζων εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Εἰ υἱὸς εἶ τοῦ θεοῦ, εἰπὲ ἵνα οἱ λίθοι οὗτοι ἄρτοι γένωνται.

records.literal_gloss: And having come the tempting [one] said to him, If son you are of the God, say that the stones these loaves become.

en.L: And the tempter came and said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "If {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are [the] Son of God, say that these stones should become loaves of bread."
en.B: Then the tempter approached {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. "If {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are the Son of God," he said, "command these stones to become loaves of bread."
en.R: The devil came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and said, "If {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are the Son of God, tell these stones to turn into bread."

es.L: Y acercándose el tentador, {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijo: «Si eres [el] Hijo de Dios, di que estas piedras se conviertan en panes».
es.B: Entonces el tentador se {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} acercó y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijo: «Si eres el Hijo de Dios, ordena que estas piedras se conviertan en panes».
es.R: El diablo se acercó a Jesús y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijo: «Si eres el Hijo de Dios, di a estas piedras que se conviertan en pan».

fr.L: Et le tentateur, s’étant approché, {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} dit : « Si {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} es [le] Fils de Dieu, dis que ces pierres deviennent des pains. »
fr.B: Le tentateur s’approcha alors de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} : « Si {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} es le Fils de Dieu, dit-il, ordonne que ces pierres deviennent des pains. »
fr.R: Le diable est venu vers {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} et {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} a dit : « Si {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} es le Fils de Dieu, dis à ces pierres de se changer en pain. »

sw.L: Na yule mjaribu akamjia, akamwambia, "Kama {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} ni Mwana wa Mungu, sema kwamba mawe haya yawe mikate."
sw.B: Kisha mjaribu alimkaribia, akamwambia, "Kama {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} ni Mwana wa Mungu, yaamuru mawe haya yageuke kuwa mikate."
sw.R: Ibilisi alimjia, akamwambia, "Kama {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} ni Mwana wa Mungu, yaambie mawe haya yageuke kuwa mkate."

ko.L: 그리고 시험하는 자가 다가와서 그분께 말하였다. "네가 하나님의 아들이라면, 이 돌들에게 빵이 되라고 말해 보아라."
ko.B: 그때 시험하는 자가 예수께 다가와 말했다. "네가 하나님의 아들이라면, 이 돌들에게 빵덩이가 되라고 명령해 보아라."
ko.R: 마귀가 예수께 와서 말했다. "네가 하나님의 아들이라면, 이 돌들에게 빵으로 변하라고 말해 보아라."

vi.L: Và kẻ cám dỗ đến và nói với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Nếu ông là Con Đức Chúa Trời, hãy nói cho những hòn đá này trở thành bánh."
vi.B: Kẻ cám dỗ đến gần {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và nói: "Nếu ông là Con Đức Chúa Trời, hãy ra lệnh cho những hòn đá này biến thành bánh đi."
vi.R: Ma quỷ đến và nói với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Nếu ông là Con Đức Chúa Trời, hãy bảo những hòn đá này biến thành bánh."

pt.L: E, aproximando-se, o tentador {{deity_pronoun:lhe|Lhe}} disse: "Se {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} és Filho de Deus, ordena que estas pedras se tornem pães."
pt.B: Então o tentador se aproximou {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}}. "Se {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} és o Filho de Deus", disse ele, "manda que estas pedras se transformem em pães."
pt.R: O diabo veio até {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} e disse: "Se {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} és o Filho de Deus, manda estas pedras virarem pão."

decisions.choice: if you are the Son of God: taking up what God has just said (3:17)
alternatives: doubting that he is the Son
decisions.reason: The form of the condition takes the statement as true for the argument. The tempter does not deny that Jesus is the Son; he urges him to use that place for himself.

decisions.choice: stones ... loaves: the round stones of the wilderness looked like small loaves
decisions.reason: Bread was baked in flat, round loaves. The stones of the Judean wilderness have the same size and shape.

decisions.choice: the devil
decisions.reason: Readable names the tempter as the devil of 4:1.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}}, {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}}, {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} on the clitic pronouns
decisions.reason: Wherever the English marks a pronoun for Jesus, the Spanish clitic standing before the verb takes the span too, as the stressed pronouns (él, ti, mí) do. Spanish leaves out a subject pronoun the English needs ("si eres"), so some English spans have no Spanish counterpart.

decisions.choice: spans only on free pronouns ({{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}})
decisions.reason: Swahili marks most pronouns for Jesus inside the verb (akamjia, akamwambia), and a prefix cannot take a capital, so only free pronouns and possessives carry the span. Swahili therefore has fewer spans than English in this chapter.

decisions.choice: the devil calls Jesus "ông" and himself "ta" (4:9)
decisions.reason: As the unclean spirits in Mark 1:24: a hostile speaker does not honour Jesus, and "ông" is the word for a man one does not honour; words of address take no deity_pronoun span. The devil's "ta" is the word of one who claims power.

decisions.choice: the devil speaks to Jesus in 해라체 with "너", through the temptation
alternatives: 합쇼체 with "당신", as the unclean spirits in Mark
decisions.reason: The devil is an open opponent who tries to make Jesus obey him; Korean lets him speak down to Jesus in the plain style (docs/korean-style.md section 4 on open opponents), unlike the spirits in Mark who cry out in fear. The narrator keeps the honorific for Jesus.

decisions.choice: tu ("tu és", "ordena", "manda")
decisions.reason: Everyone who speaks to Jesus uses "tu", his opponents and Satan too (docs/portuguese-style.md, section 4); the devil's words show his intent without a change of address.

source.text: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν· Γέγραπται· Οὐκ ἐπ’ ἄρτῳ μόνῳ ζήσεται ὁ ἄνθρωπος, ἀλλ’ ἐπὶ παντὶ ῥήματι ἐκπορευομένῳ διὰ στόματος θεοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: He then answering said, It has been written: Not on bread alone will live the man, but on every word coming out through mouth of God.

en.L: But answering, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "It is written, '{{gender:A person|Man}} will not live on bread alone, but on every word coming out through [the] mouth of God.'"
en.B: But Jesus answered, "Scripture says, 'No one lives on bread alone, but on every word that comes from the mouth of God.'"
en.R: But Jesus answered, "The Scriptures say, 'People need more than bread to live. They need every word that God speaks.'"

es.L: Pero {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, respondiendo, dijo: «Está escrito: “No vivirá {{gender:el ser humano|el hombre}} solo de pan, sino de toda palabra que sale por la boca de Dios”».
es.B: Pero Jesús respondió: «La Escritura dice: “Nadie vive solo de pan, sino de cada palabra que sale de la boca de Dios”».
es.R: Pero Jesús respondió: «Las Escrituras dicen: “La gente necesita más que pan para vivir. Necesita cada palabra que Dios dice”».

fr.L: Mais {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, répondant, dit : « Il est écrit : “{{gender:L’être humain|L’homme}} ne vivra pas de pain seulement, mais de toute parole qui sort par la bouche de Dieu.” »
fr.B: Mais Jésus répondit : « L’Écriture dit : “On ne vit pas seulement de pain : on vit de toute parole qui sort de la bouche de Dieu.” »
fr.R: Mais Jésus a répondu : « Les Écritures disent : “Pour vivre, les gens n’ont pas seulement besoin de pain. Ils ont besoin de toute parole que Dieu prononce.” »

sw.L: Lakini {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} akajibu, akasema, "Imeandikwa, 'Mwanadamu hataishi kwa mkate peke yake, bali kwa kila neno linalotoka kupitia kinywa cha Mungu.'"
sw.B: Lakini Yesu alijibu, "Maandiko yanasema, 'Hakuna mtu anayeishi kwa mkate peke yake, bali kwa kila neno linalotoka kinywani mwa Mungu.'"
sw.R: Lakini Yesu alijibu, "Maandiko yanasema, 'Watu wanahitaji zaidi ya mkate ili waishi. Wanahitaji kila neno ambalo Mungu anasema.'"

ko.L: 그러나 그분이 대답하여 말씀하셨다. "기록되어 있다. '사람은 빵으로만 살지 않고, 하나님의 입에서 나오는 모든 말씀으로 살 것이다.'"
ko.B: 그러나 예수께서 대답하셨다. "성경에 기록되어 있다. '사람은 빵만으로 사는 것이 아니라, 하나님의 입에서 나오는 모든 말씀으로 산다.'"
ko.R: 그러나 예수께서 대답하셨다. "성경에 이렇게 쓰여 있다. '사람이 살려면 빵보다 더 필요한 것이 있다. 하나님께서 하시는 모든 말씀이 필요하다.'"

vi.L: Nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} trả lời: "Có lời chép: 'Con người sẽ sống không phải chỉ bằng bánh, nhưng bằng mọi lời ra từ miệng Đức Chúa Trời.'"
vi.B: Nhưng Đức Giê-xu đáp: "Kinh Thánh chép: 'Không ai sống chỉ nhờ bánh, nhưng nhờ mọi lời từ miệng Đức Chúa Trời phán ra.'"
vi.R: Nhưng Đức Giê-xu trả lời: "Kinh Thánh có nói: 'Con người cần nhiều hơn bánh để sống. Họ cần mọi lời Đức Chúa Trời phán ra.'"

pt.L: Mas, respondendo, {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} disse: "Está escrito: 'Não é só de pão que {{gender:o ser humano|o homem}} viverá, mas de cada palavra que sai pela boca de Deus.'"
pt.B: Mas Jesus respondeu: "A Escritura diz: 'Ninguém vive só de pão, mas de toda palavra que vem da boca de Deus.'"
pt.R: Mas Jesus respondeu: "As Escrituras dizem: 'As pessoas precisam de mais do que pão para viver. Elas precisam de cada palavra que Deus fala.'"

decisions.choice: Deuteronomy 8:3: God fed Israel with manna to teach dependence on his word
alternatives: a general saying about spiritual food
decisions.reason: Moses reminds Israel that God let them go hungry and then fed them manna, to teach them that life comes from what God says. Jesus will not make his own bread; he trusts God to provide.

decisions.choice: it is written: it stands written and has authority
decisions.reason: The perfect tense speaks of Scripture as a word that still stands. Jesus answers each temptation with it.

decisions.choice: the man: a human being, anyone
decisions.reason: The word means a human being in general.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: The tempter has just spoken, so Balanced and Readable name Jesus.

decisions.choice: {{gender:A person|Man}} (L); No one (B); People (R)
decisions.reason: Literal follows the singular with the gender setting. Balanced and Readable use words that already include everyone.

decisions.choice: {{gender:el ser humano|el hombre}}
decisions.reason: Spanish has the same two wordings as English here: "el hombre" in the older sense of a human being, or "el ser humano", so Literal keeps the gender setting (meaning decision m3). Balanced ("nadie") and Readable ("la gente") need none.

decisions.choice: {{gender:L’être humain|L’homme}} (L); On (B); les gens (R)
alternatives: {{gender:L’être humain|L’homme}} at Balanced too, as Luke 4:4
decisions.reason: The word means any human being (m3). Literal keeps the singular noun under the gender setting, as in Luke 4:4, since French "l’homme" is read as "the man" more and more. Balanced follows the English "No one" with French "on", which already includes everyone and needs no setting; Readable says "les gens".

decisions.choice: mwanadamu, no gender setting
decisions.reason: "Mwanadamu" already means any human being, man or woman (meaning decision m3), so Swahili has no second wording for the English gender setting to choose.

decisions.choice: "Con người" (L, R) and "Không ai" (B), with no gender span
decisions.reason: "Con người" (a human being) already means man and woman alike, so there are not two ways of saying it to set against each other; the English "Man" has no Vietnamese counterpart that would mean the same. Lower-case "người" keeps it apart from the title "Con Người".

decisions.choice: "Có lời chép" (L); "Kinh Thánh chép" (B); "Kinh Thánh có nói" (R) for "it is written"
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the impersonal form; Balanced and Readable name the Scriptures, as the English does. The same in 4:6, 4:7 and 4:10.

decisions.choice: "사람" with no gender span
decisions.reason: The Greek means any human being (meaning decision). Korean "사람" already includes men and women, so there is nothing for the setting to change (docs/korean-style.md section 7).

decisions.choice: "성경에 기록되어 있다" (B), "성경에 이렇게 쓰여 있다" (R), through the temptation
decisions.reason: Korean needs a place where something is written; Balanced and Readable name Scripture, as the English does with "Scripture says".

source.text: Τότε παραλαμβάνει αὐτὸν ὁ διάβολος εἰς τὴν ἁγίαν πόλιν, καὶ ἔστησεν αὐτὸν ἐπὶ τὸ πτερύγιον τοῦ ἱεροῦ, καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ· Εἰ υἱὸς εἶ τοῦ θεοῦ, βάλε σεαυτὸν κάτω· γέγραπται γὰρ ὅτι Τοῖς ἀγγέλοις αὐτοῦ ἐντελεῖται περὶ σοῦ καὶ ἐπὶ χειρῶν ἀροῦσίν σε, μήποτε προσκόψῃς πρὸς λίθον τὸν πόδα σου.

records.literal_gloss: Then takes him the devil into the holy city, and set him on the pinnacle of the temple, \v 6 and says to him, If son you are of the God, throw yourself down; it has been written for that To the angels of him he will command concerning you and on hands they will lift you, lest you strike against a stone the foot of you.

en.L: Then the devil takes {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} into the holy city and set {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} on the pinnacle of the temple, \v 6 and says to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "If {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are [the] Son of God, throw {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}} down, for it is written, 'He will command {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} angels concerning {{deity_pronoun:you|You}},' and 'On [their] hands they will lift {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} up, so that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} do not strike {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} foot against a stone.'"
en.B: Then the devil brought {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to the holy city and set {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} on the high corner of the temple. \v 6 "If {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are the Son of God," he told {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "jump down. For Scripture says, 'He will put {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} angels in charge of {{deity_pronoun:you|You}},' and, 'They will catch {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} in their hands, so that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will not strike {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} foot against a stone.'"
en.R: Then the devil took Jesus to Jerusalem, the holy city. He put {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} on the highest part of the temple. \v 6 He said, "If {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are the Son of God, jump off! The Scriptures say, 'God will tell {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} angels to take care of {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. They will catch {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} with their hands so that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will not hurt {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} foot on a rock.'"

es.L: Entonces el diablo {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} lleva a la ciudad santa, y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} puso sobre el pináculo del templo, \v 6 y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dice: «Si eres [el] Hijo de Dios, échate abajo, porque está escrito: “A {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} ángeles dará órdenes acerca de {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}”, y: “Sobre [sus] manos {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} alzarán, para que no golpees {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} pie contra una piedra”».
es.B: Entonces el diablo {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} llevó a la ciudad santa y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} puso en el borde más alto del templo. \v 6 Y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijo: «Si eres el Hijo de Dios, tírate abajo. Porque la Escritura dice: “Dará órdenes a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} ángeles acerca de {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}”, y: “Ellos {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} sostendrán en sus manos, para que no golpees {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} pie contra una piedra”».
es.R: Luego el diablo llevó a Jesús a Jerusalén, la ciudad santa. Lo puso en la parte más alta del templo. \v 6 Le dijo: «Si eres el Hijo de Dios, ¡tírate abajo! Las Escrituras dicen: “Dios mandará a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} ángeles que {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} cuiden. Ellos {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} sostendrán con sus manos para que no {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} lastimes el pie con una piedra”».

fr.L: Alors le diable {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}emmène dans la ville sainte, et {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} plaça sur le pinacle du temple, \v 6 et {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} dit : « Si {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} es [le] Fils de Dieu, jette-{{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} en bas, car il est écrit : “Il donnera ordre à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} anges à {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} sujet”, et : “Sur [leurs] mains ils {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} porteront, de peur que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} ne heurtes {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} pied contre une pierre.” »
fr.B: Le diable {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}emmena ensuite dans la ville sainte et {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} plaça sur l’angle le plus élevé du temple. \v 6 « Si {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} es le Fils de Dieu, {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} dit-il, saute en bas. Car l’Écriture dit : “Il chargera {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} anges de veiller sur {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}”, et : “Ils {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} rattraperont dans leurs mains, pour que {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} pied ne heurte pas de pierre.” »
fr.R: Puis le diable a emmené Jésus à Jérusalem, la ville sainte. Il {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}a placé sur la partie la plus haute du temple. \v 6 Il {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} a dit : « Si {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} es le Fils de Dieu, saute ! Les Écritures disent : “Dieu dira à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} anges de prendre soin de {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}. Ils {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} rattraperont dans leurs mains, pour que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} ne {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} blesses pas le pied contre une pierre.” »

sw.L: Kisha Ibilisi anamchukua mpaka mji mtakatifu, na akamsimamisha juu ya ncha ya hekalu, \v 6 na anamwambia, "Kama {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} ni Mwana wa Mungu, jitupe chini; kwa maana imeandikwa kwamba, 'Atawaagiza malaika {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} juu {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}},' na, 'Mikononi [mwao] watakuinua, usije ukagonga mguu {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} kwenye jiwe.'"
sw.B: Kisha Ibilisi alimpeleka mpaka mji mtakatifu, akamweka kwenye ukingo wa juu kabisa wa hekalu. \v 6 Akamwambia, "Kama {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} ni Mwana wa Mungu, ruka chini. Kwa maana Maandiko yanasema, 'Atawapa malaika {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} jukumu la kukulinda,' na, 'Watakudaka kwa mikono yao, ili usigonge mguu {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} kwenye jiwe.'"
sw.R: Kisha Ibilisi alimpeleka Yesu Yerusalemu, mji mtakatifu. Akamweka juu ya sehemu ya juu kabisa ya hekalu. \v 6 Akamwambia, "Kama {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} ni Mwana wa Mungu, ruka chini! Maandiko yanasema, 'Mungu atawaambia malaika {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} wakutunze. Watakudaka kwa mikono yao ili usiumize mguu {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} kwenye jiwe.'"

ko.L: 그때 마귀가 그분을 거룩한 도성으로 데리고 간다. 그리고 그분을 성전 꼭대기에 세웠다. \v 6 그리고 그분께 말한다. "네가 하나님의 아들이라면, 아래로 몸을 던져라. 기록되어 있기 때문이다. '그분이 너에 대하여 자기 천사들에게 명령하실 것이다.' 그리고 '그들이 손으로 너를 들어 올려서, 네 발이 돌에 부딪히지 않게 할 것이다.'"
ko.B: 그다음에 마귀는 예수를 거룩한 도성으로 데리고 가서 성전 꼭대기에 세웠다. \v 6 그리고 말했다. "네가 하나님의 아들이라면, 아래로 뛰어내려 보아라. 성경에 이렇게 기록되어 있다. '그분이 천사들에게 명하여 너를 지키게 하실 것이다.' 또 '천사들이 손으로 너를 붙들어서, 네 발이 돌에 부딪히지 않게 할 것이다.'"
ko.R: 그다음에 마귀는 예수를 거룩한 도성 예루살렘으로 데리고 갔다. 그리고 성전 지붕의 가장 높은 곳에 예수를 세웠다. \v 6 마귀가 말했다. "네가 하나님의 아들이라면, 여기서 뛰어내려 보아라! 성경에 이렇게 쓰여 있다. '하나님께서 천사들에게 너를 돌보라고 말씀하실 것이다. 천사들이 손으로 너를 붙잡아서, 네 발이 돌에 부딪쳐 다치지 않게 할 것이다.'"

vi.L: Bấy giờ ma quỷ đem {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} vào thành thánh và đặt {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} trên nóc đền thờ, \v 6 và nói với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Nếu ông là Con Đức Chúa Trời, hãy gieo mình xuống đi, vì có lời chép rằng: 'Ngài sẽ truyền các thiên sứ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} về ông,' và 'Họ sẽ nâng ông trên tay, kẻo chân ông vấp phải đá.'"
vi.B: Rồi ma quỷ đưa {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} vào thành thánh và đặt {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} trên góc cao của đền thờ. \v 6 Nó nói với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Nếu ông là Con Đức Chúa Trời, hãy nhảy xuống đi. Vì Kinh Thánh chép: 'Ngài sẽ truyền các thiên sứ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} gìn giữ ông,' và: 'Họ sẽ đỡ ông trong tay, để chân ông không vấp phải đá.'"
vi.R: Sau đó, ma quỷ đưa Đức Giê-xu đến Giê-ru-sa-lem, là thành thánh. Nó đặt {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} trên chỗ cao nhất của đền thờ. \v 6 Nó nói: "Nếu ông là Con Đức Chúa Trời, hãy nhảy xuống đi! Kinh Thánh có nói: 'Đức Chúa Trời sẽ bảo các thiên sứ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} chăm sóc ông. Họ sẽ dùng tay đỡ lấy ông, để chân ông không bị thương vì vấp phải đá.'"

pt.L: Então o diabo {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} leva à cidade santa e {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} colocou sobre o pináculo do templo, \v 6 e {{deity_pronoun:lhe|Lhe}} diz: "Se {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} és Filho de Deus, joga-{{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} para baixo, pois está escrito: 'Ele dará ordens aos {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} anjos a {{deity_pronoun:teu|Teu}} respeito', e: 'Nas mãos {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} levantarão, para que não batas o {{deity_pronoun:teu|Teu}} pé contra [alguma] pedra.'"
pt.B: Então o diabo {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} levou à cidade santa e {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} colocou no canto mais alto do templo. \v 6 "Se {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} és o Filho de Deus", disse ele, "pula daqui. Pois a Escritura diz: 'Ele encarregará os {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} anjos de cuidar de {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}', e: 'Eles {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} segurarão nas mãos, para que não machuques o {{deity_pronoun:teu|Teu}} pé numa pedra.'"
pt.R: Então o diabo levou Jesus a Jerusalém, a cidade santa. Ele {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} pôs no ponto mais alto do templo. \v 6 E disse: "Se {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} és o Filho de Deus, pula daqui! As Escrituras dizem: 'Deus vai mandar os {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} anjos cuidarem de {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}. Eles vão {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} segurar com as mãos, para que não machuques o {{deity_pronoun:teu|Teu}} pé numa pedra.'"

decisions.choice: the holy city: Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Jerusalem is called the holy city because God's temple stood there (Isaiah 52:1; Matthew 27:53).

decisions.choice: the pinnacle: a high edge of the temple buildings
alternatives: the top of the sanctuary itself
decisions.reason: The word means "little wing", a projecting edge or corner. It may be the corner of the temple courts above the Kidron valley, a drop of well over a hundred feet. The exact place is not known.

decisions.choice: Psalm 91:11-12, quoted by the devil to make God prove his care
decisions.reason: The psalm promises God's protection to one who trusts him. The devil uses it to urge a test of that promise, and leaves out the psalm's "to guard you in all your ways". Jesus answers with another Scripture (4:7).

decisions.choice: takes, says (L); took, told, said (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration; Balanced and Readable use the past.

decisions.choice: jump down (B); jump off (R)
decisions.reason: Everyday words for the same act.

decisions.choice: Jerusalem, the holy city; God will tell his angels
alternatives: the holy city; he will command his angels
decisions.reason: Readable names the city and the speaker of the psalm.

decisions.choice: historic present at Literal (lleva, dice); pretérito at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: As in English: Literal keeps Matthew's present for past events; Balanced and Readable tell the story in the pretérito. This holds for the whole chapter.

decisions.choice: no span on a pronoun joined to the verb (échate, tírate)
decisions.reason: A clitic written onto the end of a verb cannot take a capital, so it carries no deity_pronoun span; the free and preceding pronouns in the same sentence do.

decisions.choice: historic present kept at Literal (anamchukua, anamwambia); past at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: As in John: Literal keeps Matthew's present for past events; Balanced and Readable use the narrative past (-li-, then -ka-). This holds for the whole chapter.

decisions.choice: ncha ya hekalu (L); ukingo wa juu kabisa (B)
decisions.reason: Which part of the temple is meant is uncertain (meaning decision m2); "kinara" is also a lampstand or a minaret, so the drafts describe a high edge instead.

decisions.choice: the narrator calls the devil "nó"; the devil keeps "ông" inside the psalm he quotes
decisions.reason: As for the unclean spirit in Mark 1:25, "nó" speaks of the devil without honour or abuse. The devil turns Psalm 91 into words to Jesus, so the psalm's "you" takes the devil's word for Jesus.

decisions.choice: "nóc đền thờ" (L); "góc cao của đền thờ" (B); "chỗ cao nhất của đền thờ" (R) for the pinnacle
decisions.reason: The meaning decision describes a high edge of the temple buildings; each level says it as plainly as it can.

decisions.choice: o pináculo (L); o canto mais alto (B); o ponto mais alto (R)
decisions.reason: "Pináculo" is the established Portuguese word for this spot and is kept at Literal; as the English, Balanced and Readable describe the high edge, since the exact place is unknown (m2).

source.text: ἔφη αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Πάλιν γέγραπται· Οὐκ ἐκπειράσεις κύριον τὸν θεόν σου.

records.literal_gloss: Said to him the Jesus, Again it has been written: Not you will test Lord the God of you.

en.L: Jesus said to him, "Again it is written, 'You shall not put [the] Lord your God to the test.'"
en.B: Jesus answered him, "Scripture says something else as well: 'You must not test the Lord your God.'"
en.R: Jesus answered, "The Scriptures also say, 'Do not put the Lord your God to the test.'"

es.L: Jesús le dijo: «De nuevo está escrito: “No pondrás a prueba al Señor tu Dios”».
es.B: Jesús le respondió: «La Escritura también dice: “No debes poner a prueba al Señor tu Dios”».
es.R: Jesús respondió: «Las Escrituras también dicen: “No pongas a prueba al Señor tu Dios”».

fr.L: Jésus lui déclara : « Il est encore écrit : “Tu ne mettras pas à l’épreuve le Seigneur ton Dieu.” »
fr.B: Jésus lui répondit : « L’Écriture dit aussi : “Tu ne dois pas mettre à l’épreuve le Seigneur ton Dieu.” »
fr.R: Jésus a répondu : « Les Écritures disent aussi : “Ne mets pas à l’épreuve le Seigneur ton Dieu.” »

sw.L: Yesu alimwambia, "Imeandikwa pia, 'Hutamjaribu Bwana, Mungu wako.'"
sw.B: Yesu alimjibu, "Maandiko yanasema pia, 'Hupaswi kumjaribu Bwana Mungu wako.'"
sw.R: Yesu alijibu, "Maandiko yanasema pia, 'Usimtie Bwana Mungu wako majaribuni.'"

ko.L: 예수께서 그에게 말씀하셨다. "또 기록되어 있다. '너는 주 너의 하나님을 시험하지 마라.'"
ko.B: 예수께서 마귀에게 대답하셨다. "성경에는 또 이렇게 기록되어 있다. '주 너의 하나님을 시험하지 마라.'"
ko.R: 예수께서 대답하셨다. "성경에는 이런 말씀도 있다. '주 너의 하나님을 시험하지 마라.'"

vi.L: Đức Giê-xu nói với nó: "Cũng có lời chép: 'Ngươi chớ thử Chúa, Đức Chúa Trời của ngươi.'"
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu đáp: "Kinh Thánh cũng chép: 'Ngươi không được thử thách Chúa, Đức Chúa Trời của ngươi.'"
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu trả lời: "Kinh Thánh cũng nói: 'Đừng thử thách Chúa, Đức Chúa Trời của mình.'"

pt.L: Jesus lhe disse: "De novo está escrito: 'Não porás à prova [o] Senhor, teu Deus.'"
pt.B: Jesus lhe respondeu: "A Escritura também diz outra coisa: 'Não deves pôr à prova o Senhor, teu Deus.'"
pt.R: Jesus respondeu: "As Escrituras também dizem: 'Não ponhas à prova o Senhor, teu Deus.'"

decisions.choice: Deuteronomy 6:16: as Israel tested God at Massah
decisions.reason: At Massah the people demanded water and asked, "Is the Lord among us or not?" (Exodus 17:7). To force God to act to prove his care is to test him. Jesus will not make God rescue him to show that he is the Son.

decisions.choice: the Lord: God, whose name stands in the Hebrew
decisions.reason: In Deuteronomy 6:16 the Hebrew has God's name, which the Greek Old Testament gives as "Lord". The Lord your God is the God of Israel.

decisions.choice: again it is written: Scripture set against a misuse of Scripture
alternatives: the same Scripture a second time
decisions.reason: "Again" means "on the other hand": Scripture is read in the light of Scripture.

decisions.choice: "ngươi" for the one addressed in the commandments of Deuteronomy (L, B); Readable uses "mình"
decisions.reason: As in Mark 12:30: God addresses his people through Moses with the solemn "ngươi", which is not rude in this register; Readable avoids the old pronoun. "Chúa" stands for the Greek kyrios, with no divine-name setting (style guide 7a). The same in 4:10.

decisions.choice: "주 너의 하나님" in the quotations of Deuteronomy (4:7, 4:10)
decisions.reason: The Greek quotation has "Lord" where the Hebrew has God's name (meaning decision); as in the English, the New Testament wording is followed and no divine_name span is used. "주" is the short form that stands before a name or title.

decisions.choice: tu in the quotation ("porás", "teu Deus")
decisions.reason: For the whole book: when Jesus quotes God's law, which God addresses to Israel, the quotation keeps "tu", as God's voice does throughout (docs/portuguese-style.md, section 4); Jesus's own words to the devil are in "você".

source.text: Πάλιν παραλαμβάνει αὐτὸν ὁ διάβολος εἰς ὄρος ὑψηλὸν λίαν, καὶ δείκνυσιν αὐτῷ πάσας τὰς βασιλείας τοῦ κόσμου καὶ τὴν δόξαν αὐτῶν καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ταῦτά σοι πάντα δώσω, ἐὰν πεσὼν προσκυνήσῃς μοι.

records.literal_gloss: Again takes him the devil to a mountain high exceedingly, and shows him all the kingdoms of the world and the glory of them, \v 9 and said to him, These to you all I will give, if falling down you worship me.

en.L: Again the devil takes {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to a very high mountain and shows {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} all the kingdoms of the world and their glory, \v 9 and he said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "All these things I will give {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, if {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} fall down and worship me."
en.B: Then the devil led {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} up a very high mountain and showed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} every kingdom of the world in all its glory. \v 9 "I will give {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} all of this," he told {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "if {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} kneel down and worship me."
en.R: Next the devil took Jesus to the top of a very high mountain. He showed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} all the kingdoms of the world and all their glory. \v 9 The devil said, "I will give {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} all these things if {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will bow down and worship me."

es.L: De nuevo el diablo {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} lleva a un monte muy alto y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} muestra todos los reinos del mundo y su gloria, \v 9 y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijo: «Todas estas cosas {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} daré si, postrándote, me adoras».
es.B: Luego el diablo {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} llevó a un monte muy alto y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} mostró todos los reinos del mundo en toda su gloria. \v 9 Y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijo: «Todo esto {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} lo daré si {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} arrodillas y me adoras».
es.R: Después el diablo llevó a Jesús a la cima de un monte muy alto. Allí {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} mostró todos los reinos del mundo y toda su gloria. \v 9 El diablo {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijo: «Yo {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} daré todas estas cosas si {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} inclinas y me adoras».

fr.L: De nouveau, le diable {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}emmène sur une montagne très élevée, et {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} montre tous les royaumes du monde et leur gloire, \v 9 et il {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} dit : « Tout cela, je {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} le donnerai si, tombant [à terre], {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} m’adores. »
fr.B: Ensuite, le diable {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}emmena sur une très haute montagne et {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} fit voir tous les royaumes du monde dans toute leur gloire. \v 9 « Tout cela, je {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} le donnerai, {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} dit-il, si {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} mets à genoux pour m’adorer. »
fr.R: Ensuite, le diable a emmené Jésus au sommet d’une très haute montagne. Il {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} a montré tous les royaumes du monde et toute leur gloire. \v 9 Le diable {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} a dit : « Je vais {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} donner tout cela si {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} mets à genoux devant moi pour m’adorer. »

sw.L: Tena Ibilisi anamchukua mpaka mlima mrefu sana, na anamwonyesha falme zote za ulimwengu na utukufu wake, \v 9 na akamwambia, "Haya yote nitakupa, ukianguka chini na kuniabudu."
sw.B: Kisha Ibilisi alimpeleka juu ya mlima mrefu sana, akamwonyesha falme zote za ulimwengu pamoja na utukufu wake wote. \v 9 Akamwambia, "Nitakupa {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} haya yote, ukipiga magoti na kuniabudu."
sw.R: Baadaye Ibilisi alimpeleka Yesu juu ya mlima mrefu sana. Akamwonyesha falme zote za ulimwengu na utukufu wake wote. \v 9 Ibilisi akasema, "Nitakupa vitu hivi vyote ukiinama na kuniabudu."

ko.L: 다시 마귀가 그분을 매우 높은 산으로 데리고 간다. 그리고 세상의 모든 나라와 그 영광을 그분께 보여 준다. \v 9 그리고 그분께 말하였다. "네가 엎드려 나에게 경배하면, 이 모든 것을 너에게 주겠다."
ko.B: 마귀는 다시 예수를 아주 높은 산으로 데리고 올라가서, 세상의 모든 나라와 그 영광을 보여 주었다. \v 9 그리고 말했다. "네가 엎드려 나에게 경배하면, 이 모든 것을 너에게 주겠다."
ko.R: 그다음에 마귀는 예수를 아주 높은 산꼭대기로 데리고 갔다. 그리고 세상의 모든 나라와 그 나라들의 영광을 보여 주었다. \v 9 마귀가 말했다. "네가 엎드려 나에게 경배하면, 이것을 다 너에게 주겠다."

vi.L: Ma quỷ lại đem {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} lên một ngọn núi rất cao, và chỉ cho {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} thấy tất cả các vương quốc của thế gian cùng vinh quang của chúng, \v 9 và nói với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Ta sẽ cho ông tất cả những thứ này, nếu ông sấp mình xuống thờ lạy ta."
vi.B: Ma quỷ lại đưa {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} lên một ngọn núi rất cao và cho {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} thấy mọi vương quốc trên thế giới với tất cả vinh quang của chúng. \v 9 Nó nói với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Ta sẽ cho ông tất cả những thứ này, nếu ông quỳ xuống thờ lạy ta."
vi.R: Kế đến, ma quỷ đưa Đức Giê-xu lên đỉnh một ngọn núi rất cao. Nó cho {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} thấy mọi vương quốc trên thế giới và tất cả vinh quang của chúng. \v 9 Ma quỷ nói: "Ta sẽ cho ông tất cả những thứ này, nếu ông chịu quỳ xuống thờ lạy ta."

pt.L: De novo o diabo {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} leva a um monte muito alto e {{deity_pronoun:lhe|Lhe}} mostra todos os reinos do mundo e a glória deles, \v 9 e {{deity_pronoun:lhe|Lhe}} disse: "Tudo isto eu {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} darei, se, caindo [diante de mim], me adorares."
pt.B: Depois o diabo {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} levou a um monte muito alto e {{deity_pronoun:lhe|Lhe}} mostrou todos os reinos do mundo em toda a sua glória. \v 9 "Eu {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} darei tudo isto", disse ele, "se, de joelhos, me adorares."
pt.R: Depois o diabo levou Jesus ao alto de um monte muito alto. Mostrou a {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} todos os reinos do mundo e toda a glória deles. \v 9 O diabo disse: "Eu {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} darei todas estas coisas se {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} ajoelhares e me adorares."

decisions.choice: their glory: their splendor, wealth and power
decisions.reason: Here glory is the outward greatness of earthly kingdoms.

decisions.choice: the offer: rule over the world without the way of obedience
alternatives: an offer the devil had no power to make
decisions.reason: God promised the nations to his Son (Psalm 2:8), and the risen Jesus receives all authority (28:18). The devil offers the same rule at the price of worshiping him. Matthew does not say whether the devil could give it.

decisions.choice: fall down and worship: bow to the ground as to God
decisions.reason: Here the bow is worship in the full sense, as Jesus's answer shows (4:10).

decisions.choice: a very high mountain: perhaps an echo of Moses viewing the land (Deuteronomy 34:1-4)
decisions.reason: Matthew tells of several mountains (5:1; 17:1; 28:16), but does not say so here.

decisions.choice: takes, shows (L); took, showed (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration, as in 4:5.

decisions.choice: "thế gian" (L); "thế giới" (B, R) for the world
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the key word "thế gian"; here the world means the nations and their kingdoms, so Balanced and Readable use "thế giới", the word the style guide keeps for the world as a place.

decisions.choice: historic present kept in Literal ("데리고 간다", "보여 준다", "말한다"), through Matthew 4; past in Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: As docs/korean-style.md section 3 asks; one note for the passage.

source.text: τότε λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Ὕπαγε, Σατανᾶ· γέγραπται γάρ· Κύριον τὸν θεόν σου προσκυνήσεις καὶ αὐτῷ μόνῳ λατρεύσεις.

records.literal_gloss: Then says to him the Jesus, Go away, Satan; it has been written for: Lord the God of you you will worship and him alone you will serve.

en.L: Then Jesus says to him, "Go away, Satan, for it is written, 'You shall worship [the] Lord your God and serve {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} only.'"
en.B: "Get away, Satan!" Jesus said to him. "For Scripture says, 'You must worship the Lord your God and serve no one but {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.'"
en.R: Jesus said to him, "Go away, Satan! The Scriptures say, 'Worship the Lord your God. Serve only {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.'"

es.L: Entonces le dice Jesús: «Apártate, Satanás, porque está escrito: “Al Señor tu Dios rendirás adoración, y a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} solo darás culto”».
es.B: Jesús le dijo: «¡Vete de aquí, Satanás! Porque la Escritura dice: “Debes adorar al Señor tu Dios y servir solamente a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}”».
es.R: Jesús le dijo: «¡Vete, Satanás! Las Escrituras dicen: “Adora al Señor tu Dios. Sirve solo a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}”».

fr.L: Alors Jésus lui dit : « Va-t’en, Satan, car il est écrit : “Tu adoreras le Seigneur ton Dieu, et {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} seul tu serviras.” »
fr.B: « Va-t’en, Satan ! lui dit Jésus. Car l’Écriture dit : “Adore le Seigneur ton Dieu, et ne sers personne d’autre que {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.” »
fr.R: Jésus lui a dit : « Va-t’en, Satan ! Les Écritures disent : “Adore le Seigneur ton Dieu. C’est {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} seul que tu dois servir.” »

sw.L: Kisha Yesu anamwambia, "Ondoka, Shetani, kwa maana imeandikwa, 'Bwana Mungu wako utamwabudu, na {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} peke {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} utamtumikia.'"
sw.B: Yesu alimwambia, "Ondoka hapa, Shetani! Kwa maana Maandiko yanasema, 'Umwabudu Bwana Mungu wako, wala usimtumikie mwingine ila {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}}.'"
sw.R: Yesu alimwambia, "Ondoka, Shetani! Maandiko yanasema, 'Mwabudu Bwana Mungu wako. Umtumikie {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} peke {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}.'"

ko.L: 그때 예수께서 그에게 말씀하신다. "사탄아, 물러가라. 기록되어 있기 때문이다. '너는 주 너의 하나님께 경배하고, 오직 그분만 섬겨야 한다.'"
ko.B: 그러자 예수께서 마귀에게 말씀하셨다. "사탄아, 물러가라! 성경에 이렇게 기록되어 있다. '주 너의 하나님께 경배하고, 그분만을 섬겨라.'"
ko.R: 예수께서 마귀에게 말씀하셨다. "사탄아, 썩 물러가라! 성경에 이렇게 쓰여 있다. '주 너의 하나님께 경배하여라. 오직 그분만 섬겨라.'"

vi.L: Bấy giờ Đức Giê-xu nói với nó: "Hãy lui ra, Sa-tan! Vì có lời chép: 'Ngươi phải thờ lạy Chúa, Đức Chúa Trời của ngươi, và chỉ phụng sự một mình {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} mà thôi.'"
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu bảo nó: "Hãy lui đi, Sa-tan! Vì Kinh Thánh chép: 'Ngươi phải thờ lạy Chúa, Đức Chúa Trời của ngươi, và chỉ phụng sự một mình {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.'"
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu nói với nó: "Hãy đi đi, Sa-tan! Kinh Thánh có nói: 'Hãy thờ lạy Chúa, Đức Chúa Trời của mình. Chỉ hầu việc một mình {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} mà thôi.'"

pt.L: Então Jesus lhe diz: "Vá embora, Satanás, pois está escrito: 'Adorarás [o] Senhor, teu Deus, e somente a {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} servirás.'"
pt.B: "Afaste-se, Satanás!", Jesus lhe disse. "Pois a Escritura diz: 'Tu adorarás o Senhor, teu Deus, e a ninguém servirás senão a {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}}.'"
pt.R: Jesus disse a ele: "Vá embora, Satanás! As Escrituras dizem: 'Adora o Senhor, teu Deus. Serve somente a {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}}.'"

decisions.choice: Satan: the adversary, the devil's Hebrew name
decisions.reason: Satan means adversary or accuser in Hebrew; devil means slanderer in Greek. Both name the same enemy. Jesus later uses the name for Peter when Peter opposes his way (16:23).

decisions.choice: Deuteronomy 6:13: worship and serve God alone
decisions.reason: The verse warns Israel not to follow other gods in the land. Matthew's wording has "worship" where Deuteronomy has "fear", which answers the devil's demand directly.

decisions.choice: the Lord: God, whose name stands in the Hebrew
decisions.reason: In Deuteronomy 6:13 the Hebrew has God's name, which the Greek Old Testament gives as "Lord". The Lord your God is the God of Israel.

decisions.choice: serve: serve in worship
decisions.reason: The verb is used of religious service and worship.

decisions.choice: says (L); said (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: darás culto (L); servir (B, R)
decisions.reason: The verb means serving in worship (meaning decision m4); Literal says so with "dar culto", and Balanced and Readable keep the plain "servir" as the English does.

decisions.choice: "phụng sự" (L, B); "hầu việc" (R) for serve
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads the verb as service in worship; "phụng sự" is service offered to God, and "hầu việc" is the plainer Protestant word for serving God. "Phục vụ" would sound like ordinary service.

decisions.choice: Jesus answers the devil in 해라체 ("사탄아, 물러가라")
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks to opponents in 해라체 (docs/korean-style.md section 4); the command has full authority.

decisions.choice: Vá embora, Satanás (você)
decisions.reason: Jesus addresses the devil with the "você" imperative, as he speaks to anyone (docs/portuguese-style.md, section 4); "Vai-te" is archaic. The quotation from Deuteronomy keeps God's "tu", as in 4:7.

source.text: τότε ἀφίησιν αὐτὸν ὁ διάβολος, καὶ ἰδοὺ ἄγγελοι προσῆλθον καὶ διηκόνουν αὐτῷ.

records.literal_gloss: Then leaves him the devil, and behold, angels came and were serving him.

en.L: Then the devil leaves {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and look, angels came and were serving {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: Then the devil left {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and angels came and took care of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: Then the devil left {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and angels came to take care of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

es.L: Entonces el diablo {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} deja, y he aquí, vinieron ángeles y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} servían.
es.B: Entonces el diablo {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} dejó, y vinieron ángeles y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} atendieron.
es.R: Entonces el diablo {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} dejó, y vinieron ángeles a cuidar de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.

fr.L: Alors le diable {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} laisse, et voici, des anges s’approchèrent et {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} servaient.
fr.B: Alors le diable {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} laissa, et des anges vinrent prendre soin de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.
fr.R: Alors le diable {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}a laissé, et des anges sont venus prendre soin de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.

sw.L: Kisha Ibilisi anamwacha, na tazama, malaika walimjia, wakawa wanamhudumia.
sw.B: Ndipo Ibilisi alipomwacha, nao malaika wakaja kumtunza.
sw.R: Kisha Ibilisi alimwacha, na malaika wakaja kumtunza.

ko.L: 그때 마귀가 그분을 떠난다. 그리고 보라, 천사들이 다가와서 그분을 섬기고 있었다.
ko.B: 그러자 마귀는 예수를 떠나갔고, 천사들이 와서 그분의 시중을 들었다.
ko.R: 그러자 마귀가 예수를 떠났다. 그리고 천사들이 와서 예수를 돌보아 드렸다.

vi.L: Bấy giờ ma quỷ lìa {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, và kìa, các thiên sứ đến và phục vụ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Bấy giờ ma quỷ rời khỏi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, và các thiên sứ đến chăm sóc {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Rồi ma quỷ bỏ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} mà đi, và các thiên sứ đến chăm sóc {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

pt.L: Então o diabo {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} deixa, e eis que anjos vieram e {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} serviam.
pt.B: Então o diabo {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} deixou, e anjos vieram e cuidaram {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}}.
pt.R: Então o diabo {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} deixou, e anjos vieram cuidar {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}}.

decisions.choice: were serving him: caring for him, probably with food
decisions.reason: The verb is used of serving at table and of care in general (8:15). After the fast, God provides; Jesus did not have to throw himself down for angels to come (4:6).

decisions.choice: look (L); not rendered (B, R)
decisions.reason: Matthew uses this word to point to what comes next. "Behold" is old-fashioned; Literal uses "look", and Balanced and Readable carry its force in the flow of the sentence, as in 1:20.

source.text: Ἀκούσας δὲ ὅτι Ἰωάννης παρεδόθη ἀνεχώρησεν εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν.

records.literal_gloss: Having heard then that John was handed over he withdrew into the Galilee.

en.L: Now when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} heard that John had been handed over, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} withdrew into Galilee.
en.B: News reached Jesus that John had been arrested, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went back to Galilee.
en.R: Jesus heard that John had been put in prison. So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went back to Galilee.

es.L: Y cuando oyó que Juan había sido entregado, se retiró a Galilea.
es.B: Jesús recibió la noticia de que Juan había sido arrestado, y volvió a Galilea.
es.R: Jesús oyó que habían metido a Juan en la cárcel. Por eso volvió a Galilea.

fr.L: Or, ayant appris que Jean avait été livré, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} se retira en Galilée.
fr.B: Quand Jésus apprit que Jean avait été arrêté, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} retourna en Galilée.
fr.R: Jésus a appris qu’on avait mis Jean en prison. Alors {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est retourné en Galilée.

sw.L: Basi aliposikia kwamba Yohana amekabidhiwa, alijiondoa akaenda Galilaya.
sw.B: Yesu alipata habari kwamba Yohana amekamatwa, akarudi Galilaya.
sw.R: Yesu alisikia kwamba Yohana ametiwa gerezani. Basi akarudi Galilaya.

ko.L: 그런데 그분은 요한이 넘겨졌다는 것을 들으시고 갈릴리로 물러가셨다.
ko.B: 예수께서는 요한이 잡혀 넘겨졌다는 소식을 들으시고 갈릴리로 돌아가셨다.
ko.R: 예수께서는 요한이 감옥에 갇혔다는 말을 들으셨다. 그래서 갈릴리로 돌아가셨다.

vi.L: Khi nghe rằng Giăng đã bị nộp, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} lánh về Ga-li-lê.
vi.B: Khi Đức Giê-xu nghe tin Giăng đã bị bắt, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} trở về Ga-li-lê.
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu nghe tin Giăng đã bị bỏ tù. Vì vậy, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} trở về miền Ga-li-lê.

pt.L: E, quando ouviu que João tinha sido entregue, {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} se retirou para a Galileia.
pt.B: Jesus recebeu a notícia de que João tinha sido preso e voltou para a Galileia.
pt.R: Jesus ouviu que João tinha sido posto na prisão. Por isso {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} voltou para a Galileia.

decisions.choice: handed over: arrested and imprisoned
decisions.reason: Matthew tells of John's arrest by Herod Antipas later (14:3). The same verb is used of Jesus being handed over to death (17:22; 26:2): John's path goes before his.

decisions.choice: withdrew: went away, as Matthew says when danger is near
decisions.reason: Matthew uses the same verb in 2:12-22 and 12:15. Galilee was ruled by the same Herod who arrested John, so Jesus does not go there to be safe; Matthew gives the reason in 4:14.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: A new section begins here, so Balanced and Readable name Jesus.

decisions.choice: "bị nộp" (L); "bị bắt" (B); "bị bỏ tù" (R)
decisions.reason: As in Mark 1:14: Literal keeps the Greek "handed over", which Matthew uses again of Jesus; Balanced and Readable say what happened to John.

decisions.choice: "넘겨지다" (L); "잡혀 넘겨지다" (B); "감옥에 갇히다" (R)
decisions.reason: As in the Korean Mark 1:14: Literal keeps the Greek verb, which Matthew uses again of Jesus; Balanced adds that John was arrested, and Readable says plainly where he was.

source.text: καὶ καταλιπὼν τὴν Ναζαρὰ ἐλθὼν κατῴκησεν εἰς Καφαρναοὺμ τὴν παραθαλασσίαν ἐν ὁρίοις Ζαβουλὼν καὶ Νεφθαλίμ·

records.literal_gloss: And having left the Nazareth having come he settled in Capernaum the [one] by the sea in regions of Zebulun and Naphtali;

en.L: And leaving Nazareth, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} came and settled in Capernaum, which is by the sea, in the region of Zebulun and Naphtali,
en.B: He left Nazareth and went to live in Capernaum, a town by the sea in the region of Zebulun and Naphtali.
en.R: He left Nazareth and moved to Capernaum, a town by Lake Galilee. It was in the land that once belonged to the tribes of Zebulun and Naphtali.

fr.R: Il a quitté Nazareth et il est allé habiter à Capharnaüm, une ville au bord du lac de Galilée. Elle se trouvait dans la région où vivaient autrefois les tribus de Zabulon et de Nephtali.

sw.L: Na akiisha kuiacha Nazareti, alikuja akaishi Kapernaumu, [mji] ulio kando ya bahari, katika eneo la Zabuloni na Naftali,

ko.L: 그리고 나사렛을 떠나, 스불론과 납달리 지역의 바닷가에 있는 가버나움에 가서 사셨다.
ko.B: 예수께서는 나사렛을 떠나 가버나움으로 가서 사셨다. 가버나움은 스불론과 납달리 지역의 바닷가에 있는 마을이다.

vi.B: Ngài rời Na-xa-rét và đến sống tại Ca-bê-na-um, một thị trấn ven biển, trong vùng Xa-bu-lôn và Nép-ta-li.

decisions.choice: Capernaum: a fishing town on the north shore of the Sea of Galilee
decisions.reason: Capernaum became Jesus's base in Galilee; Matthew later calls it "his own town" (9:1).

decisions.choice: Zebulun and Naphtali: the old lands of two northern tribes
decisions.reason: These tribal lands lay west of the Sea of Galilee. They were the first part of Israel to fall to Assyria (2 Kings 15:29), which is why Isaiah speaks of their darkness (4:16).

decisions.choice: by Lake Galilee
decisions.reason: The "sea" is the freshwater lake of Galilee. Readable says so.

decisions.choice: the sentence continues into 4:14 with a comma

decisions.choice: "biển" (L, B); "biển hồ" here, then "hồ" (R) for the Sea of Galilee
decisions.reason: As in Mark 1:16: the Sea of Galilee is a freshwater lake. Literal and Balanced keep "biển", the name readers know; Readable says "biển hồ" once and "hồ" after it (4:18).

decisions.choice: a full stop at the end of 4:13 in Literal
alternatives: a comma, as the English Literal has
decisions.reason: Korean puts the purpose clause of 4:14 before the main verb, so it cannot hang after a finished sentence; 4:14 begins "이는 ..." and points back, which keeps the link.

decisions.choice: à beira-mar, o mar da Galileia (L, B); o lago da Galileia (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book. As the English, Literal and Balanced keep the Gospels' "mar" and Readable says what it was, a freshwater lake. Names in their Brazilian forms: Zebulom, Naftali.

source.text: Γῆ Ζαβουλὼν καὶ γῆ Νεφθαλίμ, ὁδὸν θαλάσσης, πέραν τοῦ Ἰορδάνου, Γαλιλαία τῶν ἐθνῶν, ὁ λαὸς ὁ καθήμενος ἐν σκοτίᾳ φῶς εἶδεν μέγα, καὶ τοῖς καθημένοις ἐν χώρᾳ καὶ σκιᾷ θανάτου φῶς ἀνέτειλεν αὐτοῖς.

records.literal_gloss: Land of Zebulun and land of Naphtali, way of sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles, \v 16 the people the sitting in darkness light saw great, and to the [ones] sitting in region and shadow of death light rose to them.

en.L: "Land of Zebulun and land of Naphtali, [the] way of [the] sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles, \v 16 the people sitting in darkness saw a great light, and for those sitting in [the] region and shadow of death, light dawned on them."
en.B: "Land of Zebulun and land of Naphtali, along the road by the sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee where the Gentiles live: \v 16 the people who sat in darkness saw a great light, and for those who sat in the land of death's shadow, light rose like the dawn."
en.R: "The land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali are on the road by the sea, on the other side of the Jordan River. It is Galilee, where many people who are not Jews live. \v 16 The people who lived in darkness have seen a great light. They lived in a land where death was close, like a dark shadow. But now a light has come to them, like the sun coming up."

es.L: «Tierra de Zabulón y tierra de Neftalí, camino del mar, al otro lado del Jordán, Galilea de los gentiles; \v 16 el pueblo sentado en tinieblas vio una gran luz, y a los sentados en [la] región y sombra de muerte, una luz les amaneció».
es.B: «Tierra de Zabulón y tierra de Neftalí, junto al camino del mar, más allá del Jordán, Galilea, donde viven los gentiles: \v 16 el pueblo que estaba sentado en la oscuridad vio una gran luz, y sobre los que vivían en la tierra de la sombra de la muerte, la luz despuntó como el alba».
es.R: «La tierra de Zabulón y la tierra de Neftalí están junto al camino del mar, al otro lado del río Jordán. Es Galilea, donde viven muchas personas que no son judías. \v 16 El pueblo que vivía en la oscuridad ha visto una gran luz. Vivían en una tierra donde la muerte estaba cerca, como una sombra oscura. Pero ahora les ha llegado una luz, como el sol cuando sale».

fr.L: « Terre de Zabulon et terre de Nephtali, chemin de la mer, au-delà du Jourdain, Galilée des nations, \v 16 le peuple assis dans les ténèbres a vu une grande lumière, et pour ceux qui étaient assis dans la région et l’ombre de la mort, une lumière s’est levée pour eux. »
fr.B: « Terre de Zabulon, terre de Nephtali, le long de la route de la mer, au-delà du Jourdain, Galilée où vivent les non-Juifs : \v 16 le peuple qui demeurait dans les ténèbres a vu une grande lumière, et sur ceux qui demeuraient au pays de l’ombre de la mort, une lumière s’est levée comme l’aurore. »
fr.R: « Le pays de Zabulon et le pays de Nephtali sont sur la route de la mer, de l’autre côté du fleuve Jourdain. C’est la Galilée, où vivent beaucoup de gens qui ne sont pas juifs. \v 16 Le peuple qui vivait dans l’obscurité a vu une grande lumière. Ces gens vivaient dans un pays où la mort était tout près, comme une ombre sombre. Mais maintenant, une lumière est venue jusqu’à eux, comme le soleil qui se lève. »

sw.L: "Ardhi ya Zabuloni na ardhi ya Naftali, njia ya bahari, ng'ambo ya Yordani, Galilaya ya watu wa mataifa, \v 16 watu wanaoketi gizani waliiona nuru kubwa, na kwa wale wanaoketi katika eneo na kivuli cha kifo, nuru iliwachomozea."
sw.B: "Ardhi ya Zabuloni na ardhi ya Naftali, kando ya barabara iendayo baharini, ng'ambo ya Yordani, Galilaya wanamoishi watu wa mataifa: \v 16 watu waliokuwa wakiketi gizani waliiona nuru kubwa, na kwa wale waliokaa katika nchi ya kivuli cha kifo, nuru iliwachomozea kama mapambazuko."
sw.R: "Nchi ya Zabuloni na nchi ya Naftali ziko kando ya barabara iendayo baharini, ng'ambo ya Mto Yordani. Hiyo ni Galilaya, ambako wanaishi watu wengi wasio Wayahudi. \v 16 Watu walioishi gizani wameona nuru kubwa. Waliishi katika nchi ambamo kifo kilikuwa karibu, kama kivuli cheusi. Lakini sasa nuru imewafikia, kama jua linapochomoza."

ko.L: "스불론 땅과 납달리 땅, 바다로 가는 길, 요단 건너편, 이방인들의 갈릴리, \v 16 어둠 속에 앉아 있는 백성이 큰 빛을 보았고, 죽음의 땅과 그늘에 앉아 있는 사람들, 그들에게 빛이 떠올랐다."
ko.B: "스불론 땅과 납달리 땅, 바닷가로 난 길, 요단강 건너편, 이방 사람들이 사는 갈릴리여, \v 16 어둠 속에 앉아 있던 백성이 큰 빛을 보았다. 죽음의 그늘이 드리운 땅에 앉아 있던 사람들에게 빛이 새벽처럼 떠올랐다."
ko.R: "스불론 땅과 납달리 땅은 바닷가로 가는 길에 있고, 요단강 건너편에 있다. 그곳은 유대인이 아닌 사람들이 많이 사는 갈릴리다. \v 16 어둠 속에 살던 사람들이 큰 빛을 보았다. 그들은 죽음이 어두운 그림자처럼 가까이 있는 땅에서 살았다. 그러나 이제 해가 떠오르듯 그들에게 빛이 비쳤다."

vi.L: "Đất Xa-bu-lôn và đất Nép-ta-li, [trên] đường ra biển, bên kia sông Giô-đanh, Ga-li-lê của các dân ngoại, \v 16 dân ngồi trong bóng tối đã thấy ánh sáng lớn, và cho những người ngồi trong miền và bóng của sự chết, ánh sáng đã mọc lên cho họ."
vi.B: "Đất Xa-bu-lôn và đất Nép-ta-li, dọc theo con đường ven biển, bên kia sông Giô-đanh, miền Ga-li-lê là nơi dân ngoại sinh sống: \v 16 dân đang ngồi trong bóng tối đã thấy một ánh sáng lớn, và trên những người ngồi trong miền đất của bóng sự chết, ánh sáng đã bừng lên như rạng đông."
vi.R: "Đất Xa-bu-lôn và đất Nép-ta-li nằm trên con đường ven biển, ở bên kia sông Giô-đanh. Đó là miền Ga-li-lê, nơi có nhiều người không phải là người Do Thái sinh sống. \v 16 Dân sống trong bóng tối đã thấy một ánh sáng lớn. Họ sống trong vùng đất mà sự chết ở gần kề, như một bóng tối bao trùm. Nhưng nay ánh sáng đã đến với họ, như mặt trời mọc lên."

pt.L: "Terra de Zebulom e terra de Naftali, caminho do mar, além do Jordão, Galileia das nações, \v 16 o povo que estava sentado em trevas viu uma grande luz, e para os que estavam sentados na região e sombra da morte, uma luz raiou para eles."
pt.B: "Terra de Zebulom e terra de Naftali, junto à estrada do mar, além do Jordão, Galileia onde vivem os não judeus: \v 16 o povo que habitava nas trevas viu uma grande luz, e sobre os que habitavam na terra da sombra da morte a luz nasceu como a aurora."
pt.R: "A terra de Zebulom e a terra de Naftali ficam no caminho do mar, do outro lado do rio Jordão. É a Galileia, onde vivem muitas pessoas que não são judias. \v 16 O povo que vivia na escuridão viu uma grande luz. Eles viviam numa terra onde a morte estava perto, como uma sombra escura. Mas agora uma luz chegou até eles, como o sol quando nasce."

decisions.choice: Isaiah 9:1-2: light for the north, before the promise of a child king
alternatives: a description of the region only
decisions.reason: Isaiah promises that the land humbled first by Assyria will see a great light, and goes on to the child born to reign on David's throne (Isaiah 9:6-7). Matthew sees the light dawn as Jesus begins his work in Galilee.

decisions.choice: Galilee of the Gentiles: a region where many non-Jews lived
decisions.reason: Galilee was surrounded by Gentile lands and had many Gentile residents. The phrase points ahead to the good news for all nations (28:19).

decisions.choice: sitting in darkness, in the shadow of death: living in despair, with death near
decisions.reason: "Sit" is a Hebrew way of saying live or dwell. Darkness and the shadow of death describe a people without hope (Psalm 107:10); the light is God's salvation.

decisions.choice: the way of the sea: the region along the road toward the sea
alternatives: the coast road to the Mediterranean only
the road by the Sea of Galilee
decisions.reason: In Isaiah the phrase names a route and the land it passes through; which sea is meant is debated.

decisions.choice: light rose like the dawn (B); like the sun coming up (R)
decisions.reason: The verb is used of the sun rising. Balanced and Readable keep the picture.

decisions.choice: people who are not Jews
decisions.reason: Readable says who the Gentiles are.

decisions.choice: los gentiles (L, B); personas que no son judías (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide term for the people of other nations (meaning decision m2); Readable says it plainly, as the English does.

decisions.choice: les nations (L); les non-Juifs (B); des gens qui ne sont pas juifs (R) (for the whole book)
decisions.reason: As the term sheet, following the English per level. "Païens" now suggests unbelief or idolatry rather than simply not being Jewish.

decisions.choice: watu wa mataifa (L, B); watu wasio Wayahudi (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide term for the Gentiles as people (meaning decision m2); "mataifa" alone would mean the nations as countries. Readable says it plainly, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "dân ngoại" (L, B) for the Gentiles
decisions.reason: "Dân ngoại" is the word Vietnamese Bible readers know for peoples outside Israel, as in Mark 10:42; Readable says who they are, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "이방인들" (L); "이방 사람들" (B); "유대인이 아닌 사람들" (R)
decisions.reason: The terms settled for Gentiles in the Korean Matthew: "이방인" (L), "이방 사람" (B). Here the point is a region where many non-Jews lived (meaning decision), so Readable says that, as the English Readable does, rather than the usual "하나님을 모르는 사람들".

decisions.choice: as nações (L); os não judeus (B); pessoas que não são judias (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book (docs/portuguese-style.md, section 6): "gentios" is a church word many readers do not know; Literal keeps the word's sense "nações", and Balanced and Readable say who is meant.

decisions.choice: habitava, habitavam
decisions.reason: "Sit" is a Hebrew way of saying live (m3). Portuguese "estar sentado" cannot carry that sense, so Balanced says "habitar", which keeps the solemn tone of the prophecy; Literal keeps the picture.

es.B: Desde ese momento Jesús comenzó a anunciar: «{{plural_you:Arrepiéntanse|Arrepentíos}}, porque el reino de los cielos se ha acercado».
es.R: Desde ese tiempo Jesús comenzó a predicar. Decía: «{{plural_you:Apártense|Apartaos}} de {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} pecados y {{plural_you:vuelvan|volved}} a Dios, porque el reino de los cielos ya está cerca».

fr.L: Dès lors, Jésus commença à proclamer et à dire : « Repentez-vous, car le royaume des cieux s’est approché. »
fr.B: À partir de ce moment, Jésus se mit à proclamer : « Repentez-vous, car le royaume des cieux s’est approché. »
fr.R: À partir de ce moment-là, Jésus a commencé à prêcher. Il disait : « Détournez-vous de vos péchés et revenez à Dieu, car le royaume des cieux est tout proche. »

sw.B: Tangu hapo Yesu alianza kuhubiri ujumbe huu: "Tubuni, maana ufalme wa mbinguni umekaribia."
